start.npcText: Ah! The hill house. I'd hoped to be the first to say it properly — welcome down, and on behalf of Hollowbrook, which I am entitled to speak for, welcome down.

responses.text: Anything I should know about the roads?

the_reeve.npcText: Elected nine years running, which sounds grander than it is — nobody else will do it. I settle boundaries, I count the winter store, and I write down what was agreed so that in March nobody can say otherwise.

does_it_work.npcText: It works because I write it down. That is the entire craft. Hedda thinks I like the sound of my own voice — I do, but that is a separate matter from the ledger being correct.

she_says_that.npcText: Of course she does, she's said it to my face at three meetings. I keep her on the water committee for exactly that reason. A room where everyone agrees with me is a room where I'm about to be wrong.

responses.text: That's better sense than I expected.

village_needs.npcText: Rain, chiefly. Beyond that: the brook's dropping, and there'll be a fight about the water before the month's out. Wick wants a race dug from the deep pool. Garrow Bream's family has held that water four generations. Both of them are right, which is the worst kind of dispute.

responses.text: Can I help with any of it?

will_decide.npcText: Nothing, for as long as I can manage it. Half of reeving is knowing which quarrels solve themselves in a week of rain. If it doesn't rain I'll have to be brave, and I'd rather not.

can_i_help.npcText: You can walk the lanes and be seen doing it. I mean that seriously — this village has watched your family's windows go dark one at a time. The museum's heir on the roads, greeting people by name, is worth more than you'd think and costs you nothing but boot leather.

responses.text: Is that all anyone wants of me?

all_they_want.npcText: It's all anyone wants of anyone, at the start. The rest is earned by turning up twice. Come to the meeting at the well when I call one and stand at the front — that's two.

the_roads.npcText: Within the village, nothing worse than Bryn Thatcher's ladder. Beyond the crossroads — east of the ridge the carters are coming through with tales, and there's talk of something at the tree line above the shepherd's cot. I record talk. I don't repeat it as fact.

record_it.npcText: Two ewes gone from Orik's flock, taken up the stream. One carter refuses the ridge road after dark and won't say why, which for a carter is remarkable. That's what's in my book. Make of it what you will — and if you go up there, tell me what you see so I can write that down too.
